To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and synthesized receptors that use metal ions as negative allosteric inhibitors of hydrogen-bonding interactions with barbiturate substrats.
we have designed a receptor which is inactive in the absence of a metal ion and active in the presence of a metal ion, and we have determined the structural basis for this behavior.
the binding affinity of the barbiturate guest for the receptor was significantly enhanced when the bipyridyl moiety was replaced with a phenyl group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of artificial receptors for the recognition of biologically relevant molecules, such as barbiturates.
the design and synthesis of receptors for barbituric acid derivatives that use metal ions as allosteric inhibitors.
the design and synthesis of artificial receptors that recognize small molecules through noncovalent binding interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of barbiturates to the receptors is not inhibited by the addition of metal ions, as was predicted.
the binding of ZnII ions by the bipyridines in the receptor 7 is accompanied by a change in the receptor conformation which results in an inhibition of the binding of the barbiturate.
the design of a hydrogen‐bonding receptor with allosteric inhibition by metal ions has proven to be a difficult task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of a receptor for a specific substrate is a complex task.
the design of a receptor for barbiturates that uses metal ions as allosteric inhibitors has been successful.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to design a receptor for barbiturate substrats that is allosterically inhibited by Zn(II) ions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of the metal ion by the bipyridyl ligand results in a geometric change that inhibits the binding of the barbiturate guest by the hydrogen-bonding receptor.
the binding of the metal ions by the bipyridyl ligands in 7 causes a geometric change in 7 that results in an inhibition of barbiturate substrate recognition.
the binding affinity of a hydrogen-bonding receptor for its substrate can be modulated by the addition of an allosteric inhibitor.
